question.text: What is the maximum tenure for an auditor of a mutual fund, and what is the cooling off period for reappointment?

answer.text: Maximum 2 terms of 5 consecutive years; cooling off of 3 years
Maximum 2 terms of 5 consecutive years; cooling off of 5 years
Maximum 2 terms of 3 consecutive years; cooling off of 3 years
Maximum 3 terms of 5 consecutive years; cooling off of 5 years

explanation.text: The Logic: Mutual fund auditors may serve for not more than 2 terms of maximum five consecutive years and may be reappointed only after a 5-year cooling-off period (NISM-Series-III-C workbook, p.259). The Trap: The 3-year option swaps in a shorter cooling-off period; the source rule on p.259 specifies a 5-year cooling-off for auditor reappointment. Note: Anchor on the source-stated tenure and cooling-off rule from p.259 rather than reasoning from independence principles.
